summary: The phones run an agent's ```html-live page from the message text they already have, instead of only showing the desktop's still image. This PR adds the shared rules (src/shared/html-live-phone.ts): the phone document puts our bytes first (the CSP meta, the guard script, the libraries on iOS, the theme, the import map and the size reporter) so no page byte runs before the CSP; the phone CSP allows only the page's own origin (Android), data: and blob:, with default-src, form-action and base-uri 'none'; the guard removes RTCPeerConnection, webkitRTCPeerConnection, RTCDataChannel, Notification and service worker registration, reports CSP violations, and caps page console output at 50 lines a second, with a separate budget for its own height and blocked lines; htmlLivePhoneVerdict refuses an open fence, the desktop cap and library list, and mermaid (desktop only); phoneLiveRunning gives one slot to the full-screen view or the most visible page once the list is still for 300 ms, needs Run on a phone under 3 GB RAM and after a crash, and blocks a key after two crashes; the iOS message parser reads only {t:'h'|'e'|'b'} under 1 KB, and a per-second gate caps reads at 100. Accepted rest risk (user decision 2026-10-29): CSP does not cover WebRTC, and a page can take a clean RTCPeerConnection from an about:blank iframe, so it can reveal the phone's IP over STUN. The page holds nothing the agent could not already send from the desktop. Revisit if a page ever holds data the agent could not send itself. No UI yet: every phone surface is staged behind phone_html_live_run, off by default. Libraries: chart.js, d3, three and OrbitControls ship in both apps (about 1.2 MB raw). Android takes resources/sb-live as an assets folder, so each is an asset at its /_sb/ path next to its licence. The Expo app gets .sblib copies in apps/mobile/assets/live-libs (metro takes no .js asset), written by scripts/build-visual-host.mjs; nothing requires them until the iOS view, so they are not in the bundle yet. Mermaid does not ship on phones. Android (plan PR 4): with Settings > Labs "Run live pages" on (phone_html_live_run, BuildConfig.PHONE_HTML_LIVE_RUN default false, stored per device), a closed html-live block that passes the phone verdict runs in place of its still image. The WebView has every setting in the design's lockdown table, no JavaScript interface, third-party cookies off and a per-run https://<token>.sb-live.invalid origin served from shouldInterceptRequest: the document once with the CSP, nosniff and no-store headers (a second request is a reload: 404 and the page stops), the shipped libraries from the assets, and an empty 403 for everything else. Every navigation is refused and nothing goes to an Intent; window.open, permissions, location, file choosers and JavaScript dialogs are refused; SSL errors cancel. Height, errors and blocked URLs come only from the console, at most 100 lines a second. One page runs at a time: the full-screen view, else the most visible card once the list is still for 300 ms; a phone under 3 GB RAM or a low-RAM device waits for Run. Inline frames take no touches: a tap opens the full-screen view with the page title and "Live page from the agent". A lost renderer, an unresponsive renderer, a reload or no height within 8 s destroys that one WebView and shows the still image with Run again; after two stops a key does not run again this app run. A missing WebView shows the still image. A page that loads mermaid shows the still image and a note.

desktop.reason: The desktop already runs html-live pages in its own sandbox (src/main/ide/html-preview-*). The phone rules add an optional import map argument to htmlLiveHead; the desktop passes none and its document is byte for byte unchanged (tests/unit/html-live.test.ts).

automated: tests/unit/html-live-phone.test.ts: the CSP meta comes before every page byte for a fragment, a full document, a script before <head> and a <head> inside a comment, with and without inlined libraries; a leading doctype is removed; iOS inlines only the named libraries (classic as scripts, three and OrbitControls in the import map, mermaid never); every fetch directive refuses https, LAN, loopback, ws, wss, file:, content:, intent: and another page's origin on both origins; the verdict, run slot, low-RAM rule, crash rule, message and console parsers and the rate gate; the fixture equals the builder.

tests/unit/html-live-phone-sandbox.test.ts (headless Chromium, run here with SB_CHROMIUM set to Playwright's chrome-headless-shell 1248): a probe page tries fetch (internet, 10.0.2.2, 127.0.0.1), XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon, a worker, (internet, LAN, file:), CSS url(), @import, @font-face, a stylesheet link, preload and prefetch, an iframe, an object, a video, a script and a form post. With the Android header CSP on https://tok.sb-live.invalid and with the meta CSP alone on an opaque page, no request reaches the network layer and no WebSocket opens; fetch, XHR and both RTCPeerConnection names throw; the guard reports blocked URLs. A copy of the CSP with connect-src and img-src set to * fails the test (ten requests leak). A three page imports data: modules through the import map. A page that writes 60 error lines in its first second still reports its height (the height and blocked lines have their own budget), the bridge gets only {t,v} reports, at most 50 page lines a second, a log of a null-prototype object does not throw, and the engine reports no error for the CSP itself.

tests/unit/visual-host-asset.test.ts: the .sblib copies are exactly the libraries the phones ship (all but mermaid) and equal resources/sb-live byte for byte. Android LiveLibraryAssetsTest (Robolectric): each library and licence opens as an asset at its /_sb/ path with the vendored bytes.
npm run typecheck and npm test pass.

notExercised: Android device check: LivePageProbeTest (apps/android/app/src/androidTest) compiles but has not run on a device. It loads a probe page that tries fetch, XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, sendBeacon, , CSS url(), @import, @font-face, file:, content:, RTCPeerConnection, window.open, location, intent:, market:, meta refresh and a form post, counts connections on a loopback ServerSocket and blocks any started activity; it fails on any LEAK. It must pass on an old (2 GB) and a current device before the flag turns on. Peak memory with dumpsys meminfo, the endless-loop page and the memory-hog page are not measured.

Android rest risk T3, accepted by the user on 2026-10-29: CSP does not cover WebRTC, and the guard script that removes RTCPeerConnection is best effort. A page can take a clean RTCPeerConnection from an about:blank iframe and send STUN over UDP, which can reveal the phone's IP. The probe records this path as rtc-iframe and does not fail on it.
The iOS live view is not built yet (plan PR 5).
The Chromium sandbox test is skipped where no Chromium is installed (CI has none); it ran on this Mac.
Android System WebView and WKWebView may differ from desktop Chromium; the instrumented device probe (plan PR 4) and an iPhone probe run are the proof for each phone.
The WebRTC rest risk through an about:blank iframe is accepted, not tested.

The phones have no third-party notices screen. The Android APK carries licence files for chart.js, d3 and three (three's covers OrbitControls). The iOS bundle carries the vendored source headers where present: chart.js and three have licence headers, d3 has a copyright header, and OrbitControls has none. A notices screen is not built.
